title: Minimum Number of Flips to Convert Binary Matrix to Zero Matrix
summary: Given a m x n binary matrix, determine the least number of steps needed to convert it into a zero matrix by flipping a cell and its four neighbors, or return -1 if impossible.
statement: Given a m x n binary matrix, determine the least number of steps needed to convert it into a zero matrix by flipping a cell and its four neighbors, or return -1 if impossible.
constraints: mat has one to three rows and columns and contains only zeroes and ones.
One move flips a selected cell plus each existing edge-neighbor.
Return the fewest moves to reach all zeroes, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Encode the small matrix as one bitmask.
Precompute the XOR mask produced by selecting every cell.
Breadth-first search bitmask states; each edge is one flip.
BFS visits states by move count, so its first zero state is optimal.
editorial: There are at most 2^9 matrix states. Encode each cell as one bit and XOR the five-cell move mask to produce a neighbor. Breadth-first search from the input state therefore explores every reachable flip sequence in nondecreasing length. The independent oracle enumerates every subset of cell flips; flipping twice cancels, so a shortest solution never needs a cell twice.

tests.explanation: Three cross-shaped flips can clear the lone one.
The matrix is already zero, so no move is needed.
